characters.name: Bugs "Wabbit" Bunny
characters.description: The Ace: After a stint as a cynic, Bugs is back to his better-knownKarmic Tricksterrole — though he's notquiteas invincible as he was back in the old days. Adaptational Heroism:The original pitch for the series, first created as aDarker and EdgierPG-13 theracial cartoon, had Bugs be an out rightVillain Protagonist.For example, one of his “tricks” for fighting against Death is to put a fish in his robe and let a bear enter his robe through his backside. While no too graphic in the official episode, the act in the short bears rathergruesomeimplications, all while hesits back, watches with popcorn and quips “well, this feels barely legal. The short ends with the reveal that Bugs is destined to go to Hell for his behavior in the old classic shorts, includingthe BlackfaceinAny Bonds Today?Only for the devil himself topush him back to life, finding himtoo annoying for his taste.Needless to say, even at his most sadistic, Bugs is no where near as cruel in the official series. Beleaguered Assistant: Whenever Bigfoot is around, Bugs is demoted into this role. Berserk Button: Nothing sets him off faster than seeing/hearing someone do harm to other rabbits. Beware the Nice Ones: Bugs is a friendly guy, but when someonereallypushes him too far he can be terrifying.

characters.name: Squeaks the Squirrel
characters.description: Big Eater: Squeaks can sometimes be seen gathering or eating food. Canon Foreigner: While there have been squirrel characters in Looney Tunes before, Squeaks is a whole new cloth. Civilized Animal:ZigzaggedwithPartially Civilized Animal. Squeaks can be seen in some scenes residing within Bugs's home on the couch, watching TV upright and munching on nuts in a bowl. In the same short, however, he's prone to scavenging for nuts and remain in mostly common squirrel positions for movement and stationary moments. The only consistent trait is hislack of ability to verbally speak, opting to communicate with squeaking and pantomiming. A Day in the Limelight: "Big Troubles" is the most Squeaks-focused short so far (after mostly playing second fiddle to Bugs in most shorts, at times not being essential to the plot). Speech-Impaired Animal: He cannot verbally speak resorting to him to say in squeaks. Although there is one episode in which he can do it.

characters.name: Bigfoot
characters.description: Absurd Phobia: He's afraid of leaves. Accidental Misnaming: He keeps referring to Bugs as "Lady". And Call Him "George": Unfortunately for Bugs, he's a hugger (and a kisser). Big-Hearted Bigfoot: He never means any harm, no matter how much he causes it. Cloudcuckoolander: Extremely odd and utterly clueless.

characters.name: Yosemite Sam
characters.description: Adaptational Ugliness: This version of Yosemite Sam is much pudgier, with smaller eyes and an even bigger nose. Angrish: Usually mixed in his Southern-styled vernacular. Butt-Monkey: His abuse from Bugs reaches extreme heights. Crazy Cat Lady: Considering that he lives alone and has pet cats, a case of cat figurines, and pictures of cats, he can be considered a male version of this trope. A Day in the Limelight: "Sam and the Bullet Train", which focuses on Sam's attempts to rob the titular train.

characters.name: Wile E. Coyote
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: Sort of. He is a bit of a jerk, full of himself and motivated to show how much smarter he thinks he is, but he doesn’t try to kill and eat Bugs like he did in the classic shorts (except in "Appropriate Technology", when he briefly goes feral from hunger). Butt-Monkey: Tied with Yosemite Sam on this. Complexity Addiction: In "Leaf It Alone" he uses overly complex methods to get a leaf off his lawn when he could just pick it up. In general, he will always prefer to do things in the most complicated and technologically sophisticated way possible. A Day in the Limelight: "Leaf It Alone", "Bugs in the Garden", "Aromatherapest", "Appropriate Technology", and "Mooch Housin' Syndrome" feature Wile E. in a primary role. Deadpan Snarker: Often makes dry comments towards Bugs.

characters.name: Sir Littlechin
characters.description: A knight often on the hunt of a mythical creature of some sort. Unfortunately for him, said mythical creature usually ends up turning to Bugs for help. Butt-Monkey: He gets grand proclamations and bombastic entrances reliably culminate in sight‑gag pratfalls—tangled armor, bolting steeds, and unexpected KO’s that turn his chivalric bluster into punchline. Catchphrase: “Tally-ho!”, whenever be entrances and charges across his hunts and fairground antics or foes. Defeat Means Friendship: While he didn't actively try to harm or berate Bugs like most examples listed, he didn't appreciate Bugs and Squeaks' constant interloping (his last straw had him attempt to kill the two after the dragon escapes). Once Bugs foiled his plans of killing a local dragon, he ends up making some casual peace with him and Squeaks.He also befriends the dragon after it saves him from falling to his death. I Call It "Vera": His sword, Dirk, is apparently his best friend. Daffy mocks him for this extensively.

characters.name: Squint Eatswood
characters.description: A beaver who believes he owns an entire lake. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Does not return for the retooled seasons. Fantastic Racism: He bans everybody who isn't a beaver from the lake. He even bans fish from the lake. No Celebrities Were Harmed/Punny Name: As his name suggests, he'sClint Eastwoodas a beaver.

characters.name: Cal
characters.description: Catchphrase: "You're in my zone. My Cal-zone!" Jerkass: Sometimes, he'll be depicted as something other than an athlete, but he'll have the exact same personality. Jerkass Has a Point: Though Cal in "For the Love of Acorns" was being a jerk, Bugs and Squeaks were trespassing on the field, vandalizing property and interrupting a game. Jerk Jock: He's depicted playing all kinds of sports and usually gets cheers for his efforts, but he always has the same obnoxious, egotistical attitude. Overly Long Name: His full name is "Vladimir Angelo Chafong ReginaldMcMurthy".

characters.name: Shameless O'Scanty
characters.description: A leprechaun who often finds himself short on luck and needing some more, which he usually intends to get by taking Bugs' feet. Butt-Monkey: Shameless’s frantic quests for luck always end with him spectacularly outwitted and physically humiliated—pantsing, pratfalls, and snapped traps. Leprechaun: He is one. Lucky Rabbit's Foot: If he didn't believe in this trope, his episodes wouldn't have happened.

characters.name: The Grim Rabbit
characters.description: Adaptation Explanation Extrication: In the unfinished shortYour Bunny or Your Life, he was hunting Bugs down to send him to hell forOld Shamemoments in earlier cartoons. The series doesn't give an explanation for why he's targeting Bugs. Animal Motifs: He has some noticeable rabbit traits (rabbit ears, feet, and a carrot scythe). Breakout Character: Widely considered one of the most popular new antagonists of the series. He is so far the onlyNew Looney Tunescharacter to get a reference in alater installment. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Similar to Squint, he is absent for the retooled seasons. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: When he saw his wife about to be killed, he jumps in to save her.

characters.name: Vice President Leslie P. Lilylegs
characters.description: Affably Evil: There are times where he is generally polite. Art Evolution: He had a slightly different design in his first appearance, most notably being slightly taller and having large jowls, being simplified later on, most notably getting rid of the jowls. Bizarre and Improbable Golf Game: Tries to pull one on Bugs in "Bugs Over Par". Naturally it all backfires. Butt-Monkey: Even before Bugs or Daffy show up he gets treated like dirt by whoever he works for. Evil Cannot Comprehend Good: In one short he is his grandchildren's second favourite grandfather, and he goes through elaborate schemes to make himself the favourite so they'll take him on a trip.When Bugs suggests his grandkids might like him more if he were just nicer, he doesn't understand.

characters.name: Barbarian
characters.description: Barbarian Longhair: Although his regular hair isn't too long, his beard is massive, and they're both rather unkempt.

characters.name: Krakos
characters.description: Because You Were Nice to Me: He defended Bugs to his abusive owner near the end of "Bugsbarian" after the former helped freed him bejng chained by said owner. Berserk Button:He doesnt like his weight being insulted when Bugs mistaken him as Rudolph and thinking he gained weight in "Bugsbarian"He punches Sir Littlechin multiple inside The Grim Rabbit's body when the knight made bear puns mistaken them as "The Hooded Bear". He doesnt like his weight being insulted when Bugs mistaken him as Rudolph and thinking he gained weight in "Bugsbarian" He punches Sir Littlechin multiple inside The Grim Rabbit's body when the knight made bear puns mistaken them as "The Hooded Bear". Butt-Monkey: Krakos gets treated like a blunt instrument or steed. Doesnt help that his owner doesnr treat him better tham Bugs does.

characters.name: King Thes
characters.description: The hungry king of the beasts who often tires of his usual diet and sets his eyes out on consuming our hero. Panthera Awesome: He's a lion who's king of the jungle. Running Gag: His thick lisp means he usually has to spell his name out to properly introduce himself, lest he be mistaken for "Theth".

characters.name: The Winter Stag
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Personification: Of Winter. Elmer Fudd is able to make Summer last longer by capturing him. Deadpan Snarker: When not outright angry at Bugs for interfering with him, he has a very dry sense of humor. Defeat Means Friendship: His first appearance ends with him and Bugs having drinks and enjoying a summer's day. Good Thing You Can Heal: Bugs accidentally knocks his antlers off once. The Stag was able to regrow them, but it still made him mad. An Ice Person: Can freeze anything with his antlers.

characters.name: Jack
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome:Word of God(in this case, storyboard artist Michael J. Ruoco)saysthat he was dropped from the show after only two appearances because his personality traits (including his screaming) were deemed too similar to Yosemite Sam. New Job as the Plot Demands: He was a dog trainer in "Wabbit's Best Friend" and a painter in "Painter Paint Hare". He wasn't particularly good at either job. Ruoco again:The idea was that Jack was, well, a "jack" of all trades, but a master of none. Every time you’d see him in a new cartoon, he’d have a different profession (a painter, a dog trainer, etc.), but he’d be terrible at it, to the point he’d get frustrated and lash out, usually at Bugs.

characters.name: Scarecrow
characters.description: Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: For some reason,whenever the Scarecrow's head is detached from any form of a body, he's a timid weakling just trying to do his job.When he's attached to a body, he becomes a verycrude,determinedlegitimate threat for Bugs to handle.Especially when he becomes a giant monster made of farm equipment and hay. One-Winged AngelOnce his head merged with the local hay and farm equipment, he becomes a giant monster to take on the local intruder, Bugs. Scary Scarecrows: His more timid side wants to be this; his more competent personalityisthis.

characters.name: Claudette Dupri
characters.description: Ascended Extra: The New Looney Tunes retool promotes her from one of Bugs' minor antagonists to the co-main character of a spy format of cartoons with Pepe Le Pew. Character Development: Beginning with "The Towering Hamsterno", she more or less gets over with Pepe joining her on her missions. Cunning Like a Fox: At the very leastviews herself as such. She meets her match upon meeting Bugs however. A Day in the Limelight: Her premiere episode ("The Spy Who Bugged Me") mainly focused on her (failed) escapades trying to retrieve a bag holding U.S. government secrets from an oblivious Bugs. Bugs himself was secondary to the plot. Femme Fatale: Although she is rendered completely inept by Bugs, she is a far more even match when paired against Pepe Le Pew.

characters.name: Rock Hardcase
characters.description: Fake Muscles:After getting his muscles punctured, Rock is revealed to be a scrawny goat. The Reveal:Earlier on in "Bugs of Steel", Rock's sports drink and fitness program turned out to be a money-making scam. Later, his muscle-bound physique turned out to be fake as well.

characters.name: Hazmats
characters.description: Affably Evil: Their ruthless hunting of Bigfoot aside, they seem like pretty chill guys. Goldfish Poop Gang: Very rarely has the Hazmats' appearances been a legitimate threat to Bugs in terms of cunningness. The Guards Must Be Crazy: A pretty big issue that plagues any of the Hazmats. Mooks: They can be seen working in a multitude of positions, always filling this role for their employer. The Pollyanna: All of them try to convince each other to look on the bright side, even when they make lousy shots. They even talk to each other about their personal lives like "how's the family?"

characters.name: Viktor
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: Not him (perhaps) but his trio of fans, who swoon on him (until the tables are turn and change to who's doing better). No Celebrities Were Harmed: His appearance on "AbracaWabbit", where he's based onCriss Angel.

characters.name: Tad Tucker
characters.description: Bad People Abuse Animals: Him obsessing in eating rabbits along with eating Koala chips, Dingo jerky and Spicy Emu meat should have been red flags. In the episodes that feature Daffy, Tad's treatment towards the animals is put on full display as he assaults them and he instigates a fight between a couple of them just to provide cheap entertainment for his videos.Bugs:Hmm. Maybe I'm bein' a little too hard on dis guy.Tad:I'm so hungry. I sure could go for a family a' rabbits right about now.Bugs:Nope, I'm not. Break the Haughty: Bugs would make it his mission to burst Tad's bloated ego which always leads to TadScreaming Like a Little Girland receiving ALOT of bodily harm. Dirty Coward: Among the various ways that Bugs messes with him in "Tad the Bachelor" is faking the appearance of a shark during a swim. Tad immediately tried to use the woman he was with as a human shield, all while shouting, "EAT HER FIRST!" Failed a Spot Check: He never seems to notice Bugs whenever he's close behind him. Gaslighting: A common tactic Bugs does to Tucker is obstructing his videos (usually by bodily harm) without ever once revealing himself.

characters.name: Dr. Clovenhoof
characters.description: Advertised Extra: Despite thePromotion to Opening Titleswhen the series was revamped , he only appears in "Quantum Sheep" of season 2 and didn't make another appearance after that. Bungling Inventor: Most of his inventions don't actually work the way they're supposed to, which often causes Bugs a lot of trouble. I Just Want to Have Friends: He resorts to essentially kidnapping Bugs on a regular basis because he doesn't know any other way to make friends. Not Evil, Just Misunderstood: While he serves an antagonistic role in Bugs' life, he isn't flat out evil, he just has poor social skills and a tendency to accidentally harm Bugs with his inventions. Teleportation: His preferred method of inviting Bugs to his place is to involuntarily teleport Bugs out of his house.

characters.name: Slugsworthy the First
characters.description: An egotistical Elephant Seal who always has to be the first. It's All About Me: He always has to be the first at everything. When he runs a resturaunt, that means he's the first of his guest to eat their food.

characters.name: Daffy Duck
characters.description: Bond One-Liner: He's fond of them to the point ofBreaking the Fourth Wallto get one more in before the cartoon ends. Butt-Monkey: Despite his personality mostly being brought back to his screwy roots, he still tends to suffer a lot of injuries for the audience's amusement in several episodes, most notably anytime he's paired with the Martin Brothers as he's always bound to end suffering tons ofAmusing Injuriesat the hands of the duo unintentionally. Catchphrase: "WOOHOO! WOOHOO! WOOHOOHOOHOOHOOHOOO!" Character Check: While odd revivals beforehand have made checks to his earlier wackier self, the egotisticalButt-MonkeyDaffy was commonly the contemporary version. The show however straight up usesTex Avery's original "screwball" Daffy in full form. That said, there's episodes where his egotisticalButt-Monkeyself is most prominent (Such as any episode pairing him with the Martin Brothers) Cloudcuckoolander: This version is back to his originaldaffyand insane personality of his early shorts.

characters.name: Porky Pig
characters.description: Adaptational Ugliness: This Porky is much fatter as a deliberate homage to his original design in his earlier appearances, where he was notably more tubby. Big Fun: He is noticeably a bit tubbier, similar to his original design from 1935. Butt-Monkey: To Daffy Duck's antics. Determinator: He's endlessly patient when it comes tohelping Bugs. Foil:Whenever he's in an episode with Bugs, Porky'sBoring, but Practicalapproach to things will be too boring for an impatient Bugs, who will then recklessly get himself into trouble, turning Bugs into aButt-Monkeywhile Porky continues on unharmed in hisBoring, but Practicalways.The same applies to any time he's paired up with Daffy as his sidekick/partner, Daffy will inevitably end up at the mercy of severalAmusing Injuriesdue to his own recklessness and jerkassery, while Porky will come out unscathed.A few shorts have him alongside Petunia, who is loud, energetic, and reckless in contrast to his soft-spokenBoring, but Practicaldemeanor.

characters.name: Elmer Fudd
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: He at least got one when he helps Bugs to save the day. Affably Evil: Whenever he is an antagonist he is usually running a seemingly nice operation that underscores his own selfish motives, such as hiring Bugs to work in his petting zoo "to bring happiness to all the children", but treating the animals like prisoners during non working hours. Bald of Evil: Depends if he happens to be the antagonist of the episode. Depending on the Writer: He's been a selfish (if not outright mean) antagonist to Bugs, an innocent (or not-so-innocent) victim of Daffy's insanity, the Obi-Wan type inStar Warsparodies, and a Blofeld-esque supervillain to Pepé and Claudette. Elmuh Fudd Syndwome: Of course! He's Elmer Fudd, after all.

characters.name: Pepé Le Pew
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: In this incarnation, he is a secret agent. Adaptational Nice Guy: HisStalker with a Crushtendencies are replaced with a flirty personality more akin to James Bond. Likewise, he does not harass Claudette like he did to Penelope. Badass in a Nice Suit:Sounds familiar? Half-Dressed Cartoon Animal: This incarnation has Pepe wearing a maroon jacket. Prehensile Tail: Same as Claudette.

characters.name: Marvin the Martian
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: Or at least Adaptational Less Villainy. His first appearance in the show involves attempting to conquer Earth rather than destroying it. Aliens Are Bastards: He's still as villainous as he was in the original shorts, even if his ultimate goal this time is not toblow up the Earth, but to subjugate it.

characters.name: Gabby Goat
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: Gabby is an obscure character who hasn't been seen in the franchise since1937, and "Gettin' Your Goat" marks his long-belated return to the franchise. Butt-Monkey: He suffers greatly at the hands of Porky Pig despite his best intentions, even if it's just Porky giving him a massage. The Cynic: He's bitter and mean, and was the least enthusiastic member about being part of the "Tweet Team". Deadpan Snarker: This incarnation has a dry sense of wit. Likely done to make him less annoying than in his original 1930s appearances. Hair-Trigger Temper: An 80-year absence from the franchise hasn't done anything to sweeten his disposition.

characters.name: Tazmanian Devil
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: He's an old friend of Bugs! Dancing Tropes: Taz loves to dance when he hears the sound of castanets. Dumbass No More: He's gone from a slobberingSpeech-Impaired Animal(who was Bugs and Daffy'spetin theprior incarnation) to a respectable guy with a desk job who's a match for Bugs in the wit department. Hidden Depths: "Office Rocker" shows that Taz had a job in order to support his family but since he is fired, he reverts back to being feral ever since. Soul-Crushing Desk Job: His professional responsibilities have himverystressed.

characters.name: Lola Bunny
characters.description: Barefoot Cartoon Animal: As with her other incarnations. Composite Character: This incarnation of Lola is shown to regain hersportinessthat was first seen inSpace Jambut also the bubbly nature that was shown in her characterization inThe Looney Tunes Show. A Day in the Limelight:Lolais the main character in "Lola Rider" and "Rhoda Derby". Designated Girl Fight: Both of her starring shorts have her up against the female antagonist Rhoda. Genki Girl: Energetic and peppy, alsoHot-Bloodedon occasion.

characters.name: The Martin Brothers
characters.description: Achievements in Ignorance: They achieve a lot while being blissfully ignorant of everything going on around them. The Bus Came Back: The first time in years these guys have a role beyond background appearances or cameos. Oblivious to Hatred: To Daffy, who hates their guts while they remain entirely oblivious to Daffy's dislike of them. A Taste of Their Own Medicine: An unintentional example. Daffy usually heckles others for no good reason. These guys deliver the same kind of grief he does all unintentionally.

characters.name: Sniffles
characters.description: Cast as a Mask: Literally. HisDarkBatguise is voiced by Daran Norris. The reveal features a back-and-forth shift, as he keeps taking the mask off and on.Sniffles:Pretty cool, huh?Minnesota Rats:It was until you took the mask off. Casting Gag: Kath Soucie had previously voiced Li'l Sneezer (a deliberate counterpart to Sniffles) onTiny Toon Adventures. Motor Mouth: As Minnesota Rats says, a nice kid that never knows when to shut up. Took a Level in Badass: Sniffles takes on a Batman-like superhero alter-ego calledDarkBat.

characters.name: Foghorn Leghorn
characters.description: Adaptational Jerkass: Foghorn wasn't exactly nice to begin with (Except onThe Looney Tunes Show) but this incarnation has none of hisJerk with a Heart of Goldmoments and is simply an outright jerkass with no redeeming qualities who also takes on a more traditional antagonistic role in the vein of Yosemite Sam and Elmer Fudd. Adaptational Ugliness: Foghorn looks nothing like he did before, and has a rather hideous design. Butt-Monkey: When paired up with Daffy he's bound to end as this. Characterization Marches On: In his initial appearances, he wasn't so bad, being at worst unknowingly obnoxious (such as sitting in front of Squeaks at a movie theater and talking too loudly) and still doing legitimate business. "Free Range Foghorn" (his first major role) even has him as the protagonist, with Daffy trying to scam his farm and harass him. Afterwards, though, Foghorn would be portrayed as more of a straight-up antagonist running scams. Honest John's Dealership: Usually runs scam businesses to con people out of their money with crappy and overpriced services and products.
